# yii3-webhooks

## Install

```bash
composer require rasuvaeff/yii3-webhooks
```

## Rules

- Event id goes to the receiver as `X-Webhook-Id` and is their dedup key:
  pass `id:` (the domain event's id) when the webhook mirrors one, otherwise a
  republish arrives under a new id. Omitted => 32 random hex chars.
- No id generator is bound: `WebhookDispatcher` is an interface, so the app
  owns id policy. `WebhookDelivery::create(id:)` exists too — keep it <= 32
  chars, the column width in yii3-webhooks-db.

- Sign outbound: `HmacSha256Signer::sign(payload, secret, timestamp, eventId)` → `WebhookSignature`.
- Canonical message: `"{len(eventId)}.{eventId}.{timestamp}.{len(payload)}.{payload}"`,
  where `payload` is the exact HTTP body string. The length prefixes are what
  keeps it canonical — `.` is legal inside an event id, and without them one
  signed string parses into several different triples (an intercepted delivery
  could be re-framed around the same signature).
- Send `X-Webhook-Id: {eventId}` and `X-Webhook-Signature: t={ts},v1={hex}` headers.
- Verify inbound: `WebhookVerifier::verify(payload, secret, signature, eventId)` returns bool.
- Use `hash_equals()` internally — never `===` for signatures.
- Signing changed in 2.0: 1.x signed `"{eventId}.{timestamp}.{payload}"`. Neither
  version accepts the other's signature, so receivers need a window accepting
  both framings — legacy signer + rollout order in UPGRADE.md. roave reports the
  release clean; it compares the PHP API, not the wire.
- `WebhookDelivery` stores only `endpointUrl`, never the secret — but the URL is
  itself sensitive and NOT safe to log as-is: a query string is accepted and
  stored verbatim, so `https://host/hook?token=…` puts the receiver's credential
  in every log line. Redact query and fragment before logging.
- `WebhookEndpoint` rejects credentials in the URL and loopback/private/link-local/
  reserved IP literals (`127.0.0.1`, `10.0.0.5`, `169.254.169.254`, `[::1]`,
  `localhost`); `allowPrivateNetwork: true` opts one endpoint back in. A single
  trailing dot is the DNS root label and is stripped before the checks, so
  `localhost.`/`127.0.0.1.` are rejected too and `https://./hook` is a URL with no
  host; `getUrl()` still returns the URL verbatim. It does not resolve host names
  — the dispatcher must resolve-and-filter, refuse redirects (or re-check each
  hop) and set timeouts.
- `save()` never writes the status of a delivery that already exists — only
  `markDelivered()`/`markFailed()` ever write one. A claim writes a lease, not a
  status: the claimed delivery stays `Pending`. Otherwise a stale copy resurrects
  a finished delivery.
- More than one worker => the storage must implement `ClaimingDeliveryStorage`;
  `findPending()` hands the same rows to everyone and ignores backoff, and is not
  a fallback — no claim means run one worker.
- `markDelivered()`/`markFailed()` are a compare-and-set on `Pending` — marking a
  delivery somebody else already finished is a silent no-op, in every storage.
- `NonceStorage::add()` must be atomic and return false on duplicate nonce.
- `ReplayGuard::accept()` throws `RuntimeException` when storage rejects a duplicate nonce.
- Use event ID (from `X-Webhook-Id` header) as the nonce for replay protection.
- No HTTP client dependency — implement `WebhookDispatcher` in your adapter.

## API

### Signing (outbound)

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\HmacSha256Signer;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookEndpoint;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookEvent;

$event = WebhookEvent::create(
    type: 'order.created',
    payload: json_encode(['orderId' => 42]),
    occurredAt: $clock->now(),   // optional
    id: $domainEvent->getId(),   // optional; omitted => 32-char hex
);

$signer = new HmacSha256Signer();
$signature = $signer->sign(
    payload: $event->getPayload(),
    secret: $endpoint->getSecret(),
    timestamp: $clock->now()->getTimestamp(),
    eventId: $event->getId(),
);

// X-Webhook-Id: {$event->getId()}
$header = $signature->toHeaderValue(); // "t=1717228800,v1=<hex>"
```

`WebhookSigner` is the signing interface. Use `HmacSha256Signer` unless you need a compatible custom scheme.

### Verification (inbound)

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookSignature;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookVerifier;

$verifier = new WebhookVerifier(signer: $signer, clock: $clock, toleranceSeconds: 300);
$sig = WebhookSignature::fromHeaderValue($request->getHeaderLine('X-Webhook-Signature'));
$eventId = $request->getHeaderLine('X-Webhook-Id');
$valid = $verifier->verify(payload: $body, secret: $secret, signature: $sig, eventId: $eventId);
```

### Replay protection

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\InMemoryNonceStorage;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\ReplayGuard;

$guard = new ReplayGuard(new InMemoryNonceStorage());
$guard->isReplayed($eventId); // bool
$guard->accept($eventId);     // marks as seen; throws RuntimeException if duplicate
```

### Delivery tracking

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\InMemoryDeliveryStorage;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookDelivery;
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\WebhookRetryPolicy;

$storage = new InMemoryDeliveryStorage();
$policy = WebhookRetryPolicy::fixed(maxAttempts: 3, delaySeconds: 60);
// or: WebhookRetryPolicy::exponential(maxAttempts: 5, baseSeconds: 10, cap: 3600)

$delivery = WebhookDelivery::create(event: $event, endpoint: $endpoint); // + optional createdAt:, id:
$storage->save($delivery);

// After failed attempt:
$delivery = $delivery->withAttempt($now, error: 'timeout');
$storage->save($delivery);

if (!$policy->shouldRetry($delivery)) {
    $storage->markFailed($delivery); // always finalize exhausted deliveries
}

$policy->shouldRetry($delivery);             // bool
$policy->isReadyForRetry($delivery, $now);   // bool
$policy->nextDelaySeconds($delivery->getAttempts()); // seconds until next attempt
```

`WebhookDeliveryStorage` is the persistence interface. Core provides `InMemoryDeliveryStorage`; production code should use a persistent backend.

### Claiming deliveries (more than one worker)

```php
use Rasuvaeff\Yii3Webhooks\ClaimingDeliveryStorage;

// ClaimingDeliveryStorage extends WebhookDeliveryStorage; InMemoryDeliveryStorage
// and rasuvaeff/yii3-webhooks-db implement it. There is no fallback to
// findPending() in a multi-worker loop: it hands the same batch to every worker.
if (!$storage instanceof ClaimingDeliveryStorage) {
    throw new \RuntimeException($storage::class . ' cannot claim; run a single worker instead');
}

$batch = $storage->claimReady(
    now: $now,
    readyThresholds: $policy->readyThresholds($now), // attempts => latest ready lastAttemptAt
    maxAttempts: $policy->getMaxAttempts(),
    leaseSeconds: 300,   // must outlive the slowest attempt
    limit: 100,
);

foreach ($batch as $delivery) {
    // deliver, then leave the claim:
    //   $storage->markDelivered($delivery->withAttempt($now));
    //   $storage->markFailed($delivery->withAttempt($now, error: $e));
    // retryable failure — record the attempt and hand the lease back:
    //   $storage->save($delivery->withAttempt($now, error: $e));
    //   $storage->releaseClaim($delivery);
}
```

A claimed delivery stays `Pending`; ownership is a lease that expires, so a dead
worker strands nothing. Exhausted deliveries (`attempts >= maxAttempts`) are
claimed too — only the caller can mark them `Failed`.

### WebhookDispatcher (implement your own)

```php
interface WebhookDispatcher
{
    public function dispatch(WebhookEvent $event, WebhookEndpoint $endpoint): WebhookDelivery;
}
```
